HOI AN FOOD TOUR 2026 🇻🇳 | Best Food, Street Eats & Drinks in Hoi An, Vietnam

Welcome to our Hoi An Food Tour 2026 and Hoi An Vietnam food guide 🇻🇳 We try Hoi An street food, White Rose dumplings, Vietnamese pancakes, local restaurants, tropical drinks, market snacks and more.

This is the final video in our Vietnam travel series, and this time we’re eating our way through Hoi An.

If you're looking for the best food in Hoi An, planning a Hoi An food tour, searching for Hoi An street food, or wondering what to eat in Hoi An Vietnam, this video shares the food and drink experiences that genuinely stood out during our trip.

We start with our main Vietnamese dinner at MẸT Vietnamese Restaurant & Vegetarian Food in Hoi An Ancient Town. The restaurant sits directly opposite the river, with its front entrance opening onto the historic streets and the back overlooking the riverside.

Instead of ordering just one dish each, we shared several Vietnamese dishes so we could try more variety and compare our reactions.

One of the most interesting local specialties we tried was White Rose, or bánh bao bánh vạc — delicate steamed dumplings known for their flower-like appearance and strong connection to Hoi An.

We also tried Vietnamese pancakes, fresh juices and other shared dishes while keeping our genuine reactions and conversations in the video.

From there, we continue exploring Hoi An’s food scene, including tropical drinks, street sweets and fresh sugarcane juice.

We also visit Chợ Hội An, where one of the most interesting parts of the local dining culture is how many small food stalls sit together in one place. Diners can sit directly along the counters while dishes are prepared in front of them, making the experience feel completely different from a normal restaurant.

Another drink that caught our attention was a popular Hoi An herbal drink with its distinctive lotus-style presentation — the kind of simple local stop that often has people lining up in the Ancient Town.

At Hoi An Night Market, we walk through food stalls, watch dishes being prepared and try a few smaller snacks rather than pretending we tasted everything on offer.

We also share one practical lesson from our trip: online menus are not always up to date, so it is worth checking the current menu and prices before ordering.

Whether you're planning a Vietnam food tour, looking for Hoi An restaurants, Hoi An street food, local Vietnamese food, market food or simply wondering what to eat in Hoi An, we hope this guide gives you a few useful ideas.
